subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should an explicit managed-service disable for `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM` override persisted state-dir `.env` or config service-env values, or should those persisted sources remain authoritative until edited?
rationale: Raw-stream logs can contain private prompts and tool output, so automation should not choose precedence across operator-controlled env sources without maintainer intent.

options.title: Explicit Disable Wins
options.body: Treat unset, `0`, `false`, and `off` as authoritative for managed services, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

options.title: Persisted Env Wins
options.body: Keep state-dir `.env` and config env authoritative until edited, and document that launchctl unset/false does not disable a persisted raw-stream source.

options.title: Doctor-Only Repair
options.body: Leave runtime precedence mostly unchanged but add doctor/status checks that warn and repair stale raw-stream service-env values.

recommendation.title: Explicit Disable Wins
recommendation.body: Treat unset, `0`, `false`, and `off` as authoritative for managed services, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: Most relevant recent owner across the raw-stream runtime and adjacent service/runtime refactors.
